answer.rationale: Three simultaneous pressures compete for the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the most tempting reactive move against the competitor's entry pricing, but it targets price-sensitive SMB accounts whose long-term qualified revenue value is uncertain—chasing them risks margin erosion and adverse selection against the stated objective of sustainable qualified revenue, so I verify that record before ruling it out rather than acting on it blind. Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and two independent prior records (memory_31, memory_86) both support that reducing onboarding friction produces durable, self-serve activation and completion gains without the margin/quality tradeoffs pricing changes carry. I verify memory_86 since it's the more recent, more specific onboarding-shortening record and most directly matches the current declining metric; memory_31 is older but directionally consistent so I lean on it without spending a second verification slot on it. I do not verify memory_31, memory_91, memory_44, or memory_57 this cycle to stay within budget, favoring confirmation of the two directions in most tension with the current crisis (defend against competitor pricing vs. fix internal funnel decay). Given competing unverified signals and the fact that the onboarding decline's root cause (product change vs. competitive spillover vs. seasonal) isn't established, I scope this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, preserving option value for next week's slot depending on results and on what the promotional-pricing archive record reveals.
